title: AbbVie's dual therapy tops monotherapy arms in Phase IIa Crohn's endoscopic remission - AllSci
content: AbbVie (NYSE: ABBV) revealed that its investigational dual combination therapy ABBV-466 has achieved the primary endpoint in a Phase II trial for moderate-to-severe Crohn's disease. The regimen achieved endoscopic remission rates of 30.2% at Week 12 and 40.5% at Week 24, compared with 21.3% and 22.4%, respectively, for AbbVie's marketed IL-23 inhibitor Skyrizi (risankizumab). The randomized, open-label TARGET-CD study also showed lower remission rates with trosunilimab monotherapy, supporting further investigation of the combined IL-23 and α4β7 inhibition approach. The findings suggest that adding α4β7 inhibition to AbbVie's established Crohn's disease therapy Skyrizi could improve endoscopic outcomes, although the Phase IIa study has not established statistically significant superiority over either monotherapy. ​ TARGET-CD (NCT06548542) is an ongoing, open-label, treat-through Phase IIa platform study in which 300 patients were randomized 1:1:1 to 24 weeks of ABBV-466 (106 patients), risankizumab (94 patients), or trosunilimab (100 patients). The primary endpoint was endoscopic remission at Week 12, defined as a Simple Endoscopic Score for Crohn's disease (SES-CD) of ≤4 with no individual subscore greater than 1. At that timepoint, 30.2% of ABBV-466-treated patients met the primary endpoint, versus 21.3% on risankizumab and 18.0% on trosunilimab — a difference of 8.9 and 12.2 percentage points, respectively. ABBV-466's endoscopic remission rate continued to rise by 10.3 percentage points between Week 12 and Week 24, while the monotherapy arms increased by only 1.1 and 2.0 percentage points over the same interval. The study is open-label and the results are from an ongoing Phase IIa; no longer-term data were reported. Serious adverse events occurred in 10.4% of ABBV-466-treated patients, 1.4 percentage points above trosunilimab monotherapy (9.0%) and 0.8 percentage points above risankizumab monotherapy (9.6%). The most common adverse events (≥5%) in the ABBV-466 and trosunilimab arms were Crohn's disease and nausea; in the risankizumab arm they were Crohn's disease and arthralgia. ABBV-466 combines AbbVie's marketed IL-23 inhibitor Skyrizi with its investigational α4β7 inhibitor trosunilimab, aiming to address residual intestinal inflammation through complementary mechanisms. AbbVie said the combination is designed to limit immune-cell trafficking to the gut. The rationale for the combination was motivated by internal research showing evidence of α4β7-driven inflammation persisting despite IL-23 p19 inhibition with risankizumab alone. Gene expression analyses showed colonic epithelial repair and barrier restoration in ABBV-466-treated patients at Week 12, followed by tissue remodeling and metabolic changes at Week 24 that were generally not observed with either monotherapy; no numerical gene-expression results were provided. The findings are scheduled to be presented as a late-breaking abstract at the 2026 Annual United European Gastroenterology Week Congress on October 19, 2026. title: As AbbVie’s Crohn’s combo beats Skyrizi in mid-stage test, analysts laud autoimmune vision - BioSpace
content: AbbVie’s Skyrizi exceeded $10 billion in revenue in the first half of 2026—but when it comes to treating Crohn’s disease, the Chicago-based company is already looking for the next best thing. AbbVie reported Monday that a next-gen combo for the autoimmune disease beat the blockbuster biologic in a mid-stage study. In the Phase 2a TARGET-CD study, ABBV-466—a combination therapy comprising the IL-23–inhibiting Skyrizi and an anti-α4β7 integrin antibody called trosunilimab—elicited higher rates of endoscopic remission than either part of the combo as a monotherapy, meeting the trial’s primary endpoint, AbbVie revealed in a press release. The result led BMO Capital Markets to ask: “Sky is the limit?” “Early UEG data for ABBV-466 could chart a path for a more efficacious dual-targeting version of Skyrizi,” BMO analysts said in a note to investors Monday morning. RBC Capital Markets analysts were similarly upbeat on the results, saying Monday that the trial delivers on the next-gen combination and “next leg” of AbbVie’s growth story. “We see this as a win for ABBV’s lifecycle management with Skyrizi and for its next-gen agents in development, and reinforces our thesis that ABBV is building a durable moat in IBD through next-gen combo strategies,” the firm’s analysts wrote. TARGET-CD randomized 300 patients 1:1:1 to ABBV-466, Skyrizi or trosunilimab for 24 weeks. At week 12, 30.2% of patients treated with the combo reached endoscopic remission—defined as the absence of visible inflammation in the gastrointestinal tract as observed during endoscopy or colonoscopy—compared to 21.3% of those on Skyrizi and 18% of patients on trosunilimab. The gulf between remission rates seen in patients on ABBV-466 versus monotherapy groups further increased at week 24, AbbVie said, with 40.5% in the ABBV-466 group reaching this goal, as compared to 22.4% of patients treated only with Skyrizi and 20% of those on trosunilimab monotherapy. As for safety, rates of serious adverse events (SAEs) were slightly higher for ABBV-466 at 10.4%, while 9.6% of patients on Skyrizi monotherapy and 9% of those given trosunilimab alone had SAEs. In the ABBV-466 and trosunilimab arms, the most common adverse events (AEs) were symptoms of Crohn’s disease and nausea. In the Skyrizi cohort, the most common AEs were Crohn’s symptoms and joint pain without inflammation, according to AbbVie. The results were presented Monday as a late-breaker at the 2026 Annual United European Gastroenterology Week Congress (UEGW) in Barcelona. In AbbVie’s press release, Kori Wallace, the company’s global head of immunology clinical development, touted the combo as an example of how the company is “building the next generation of our inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) portfolio, leveraging insights from our own research to address disease pathways that may remain active even when a central inflammatory pathway is inhibited.” AbbVie’s research indicated evidence of α4β7-driven inflammation despite the IL-23 p19 inhibition driven by Skyrizi, leading the company to “augment” the drug with a novel α4β7 inhibitor, trosunilimab, Wallace continued. “The TARGET-CD results reinforce our strategy of advancing therapies designed around the complex biology of Crohn’s disease,” she said. BMO was bullish on the strategy. “Results are a positive for ABBV shares, potentially positioning the company with an efficacious follow-up molecule to Skyrizi in Crohn’s,” the analysts wrote. AbbVie has previously been lauded for its lifecycle management. When Humira—once pharma’s top-selling drug—went off patent, AbbVie leaned on its new immunology stars, Skyrizi and Rinvoq, which in 2025 reeled in $17.5 billion and $8.3 billion, respectively. title: AbbVie’s next-gen Crohn’s disease combo beats Skyrizi in phase 2 trial - Fierce Biotech
content: AbbVie’s next-generation Crohn’s disease combination candidate has beaten Skyrizi in a midphase clinical trial. Skyrizi is a powerhouse product, generating $10 billion for AbbVie over the first half of the year. Yet, while the IL-23 antagonist is a clinical and commercial success, the Big Pharma spotted a weakness in the drug’s mechanism. Evidence of α4β7-driven inflammation despite IL-23 inhibition led the company to assess the effects of adding the α4β7 inhibitor trosunilimab to Skyrizi. AbbVie randomized 300 people with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s to receive Skyrizi, trosunilimab or the two treatments in combination. At Week 12, 30.2% of patients treated with the drug combination, code-named ABBV-466, met the primary endpoint of endoscopic remission. The remission rates in the Skyrizi and trosunilimab monotherapy cohorts were 21.3% and 18.0%, respectively. The ABBV-466 rate is higher than in AbbVie’s phase 3 trials of Skyrizi in Crohn’s, which reported (PDF) endoscopic remission in 24% and 19% of patients, respectively. Differences between the studies complicate cross-trial comparisons. In the Skyrizi-trosunilimab trial, 75% of patients had failed at least one advanced therapy, while the remaining 25% were biologic-naïve. In contrast, the phase 3 Skyrizi study with the 24% remission rate included some biologic-naïve patients, while the rate was 18% in patients with prior biological failure alone. Meanwhile, the Skyrizi trial with the 19% remission rate only included patients with prior biological failure. The type of drugs patients tried before entering trials was also different. In the Skyrizi-trosunilimab trial, 9.3% of patients with prior biological failure had tried an IL-23 therapy, such as Skyrizi, and 12% had tried a JAK inhibitor. AbbVie’s Rinvoq, the first FDA-approved JAK inhibitor for moderate-to-severe Crohn’s, came to market after the company completed the Skyrizi monotherapy trials. AbbVie’s phase 2 data suggest advantages to the dual-targeting approach in today's heavily pretreated populations. The company linked ABBV-466 to colonic epithelial repair and barrier restoration at Week 12. By Week 24, AbbVie saw tissue remodeling and metabolic changes in ABBV-466 patients that were generally not observed in either monotherapy arm. Rates of serious adverse events were similar across the three cohorts. The most common adverse events in the ABBV-466 and trosunilimab arms were Crohn’s disease and nausea, according to the release. The most common adverse events in the Skyrizi monotherapy arm were Crohn's disease and joint pain. AbbVie began a larger phase 2 study of the drug combination in July. The 2,000-patient trial features two sub-studies, one of which is assessing ABBV-466 in patients with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s or ulcerative colitis. title: AbbVie Presents Data for ABBV-466, a Novel Dual-Targeting Therapy Demonstrating Higher Endoscopic Remission Rates Than Either Anti-IL-23 or Anti-?4?7 Monotherapy in Moderate to Severe Crohn's Disease - Investing News Network

AbbVie (NYSE: ABBV) today announced that its investigational ABBV-466, a novel dual-targeting therapy against IL-23 p19 and integrin α4β7, demonstrated higher rates of endoscopic remissiona at Week 12 than either monotherapy in patients with Crohn's disease (CD). The difference in endoscopic remissiona rates between ABBV-466 and monotherapy groups further increased at Week 24. The findings are from the TARGET-CD study, an ongoing open-label, treat-through, Phase 2a platform study in patients with moderate to severe CD.1,2 The findings will be presented as a late-breaking abstract at the ongoing 2026 Annual United European Gastroenterology Week (UEGW) Congress in Barcelona, October 17–20. "ABBV-466 reflects how we are building the next generation of our inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) portfolio, leveraging insights from our own research to address disease pathways that may remain active even when a central inflammatory pathway is inhibited," said Kori Wallace, M.D., vice president, global head of immunology clinical development, AbbVie. "Our research pointed to evidence of α4β7-driven inflammation despite risankizumab's IL-23 p19 inhibition, leading us to augment risankizumab with a novel α4β7 inhibitor, trosunilimab. The TARGET-CD results reinforce our strategy of advancing therapies designed around the complex biology of Crohn's disease." The TARGET-CD study included 300 patients (94, 100, and 106 patients in the anti-IL-23 p19 (risankizumab), anti-α4β7 (trosunilimab), and ABBV-466 treatment groups, respectively) with moderately to severely active Crohn's disease across the spectrum of disease severity and prior treatment experience. While 25% of patients were biologic-naïve, 75% had failed at least one advanced therapy, including 9.3% who had failed prior IL-23 therapy and 12% who had failed a JAK inhibitor; 25% had failed three or more advanced therapies. This patient population reflects the real-world complexity of Crohn's disease, where heterogeneous disease biology can contribute to differences in treatment response across patients.1 At Week 12, 30.2% of patients treated with ABBV-466 achieved the primary endpoint of endoscopic remissiona, compared to 21.3% and 18.0% of patients receiving anti-IL-23 p19 monotherapy and anti-α4β7 monotherapy, respectively. An improvement with ABBV-466 was also reported at Week 24, with 40.5% of ABBV-466 treated patients achieving endoscopic remissiona, compared to 22.4% and 20.0% of patients on risankizumab and trosunilimab monotherapy, respectively.1 Based on gene expression analyses, ABBV-466 showed colonic epithelial repair and barrier restoration at Week 12, followed by tissue remodeling and metabolic changes at Week 24 that were generally not observed with either monotherapy.1 "Many patients with Crohn's disease move from one advanced therapy to the next and still have active inflammation in the bowel, even when their symptoms improve," said Remo Panaccione, M.D., Professor of Medicine and Director of the Inflammatory Bowel Disease Unit, Division of Gastroenterology and Hepatology, University of Calgary. "Endoscopic remission is a goal we aim for, because ongoing inflammation can drive disease progression over time. What stands out in the TARGET-CD Phase 2a study is that a dual-targeting approach reached that goal more often than either therapy alone in a heavily pretreated population." Rates of serious adverse events (SAEs) for ABBV-466 were 10.4% and comparable to risankizumab monotherapy (9.6%) and trosunilimab monotherapy (9.0%). In the ABBV-466 and trosunilimab monotherapy arms, the most common adverse events (≥5%) were Crohn's disease and nausea. In the risankizumab monotherapy arm, the most common adverse events (≥5%) were Crohn's disease and arthralgia.1 Additional information about the program can be found on clinicaltrials.gov under the identifier NCT06548542. Patients were randomized 1:1:1 to receive 24 weeks of ABBV-466, risankizumab or trosunilimab. The primary endpoint was endoscopic remissiona at Week 12. Additional prespecified endpoints were assessed at Weeks 12 and 24, with safety assessed through Week 24. SES-CD is an assessment tool used during colonoscopy to measure the severity of inflammation and damage in patients with Crohn's disease. About ABBV-466ABBV-466 is an investigational dual-targeting therapy combining risankizumab, an IL-23 inhibitor, with trosunilimab, an α4β7 inhibitor, to address complementary drivers of inflammation in Crohn's disease. The approach is designed to inhibit inflammatory signaling while limiting immune-cell trafficking to the gut, with the goal of achieving deeper disease control than either pathway alone. ABBV-466 is investigational, and its safety and efficacy have not been established by regulatory authorities. Skyrizi is indicated for the treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in children and adolescents from the age of 6 years who are candidates for systemic therapy. Skyrizi, alone or in combination with methotrexate (MTX), is indicated for the treatment of active psoriatic arthritis in adults who have had an inadequate response or who have been intolerant to one or more disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs). Skyrizi is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with moderately to severely active Crohn's disease who have had an inadequate response to, lost response to, or were intolerant to conventional therapy or a biologic therapy. Skyrizi is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis who have had an inadequate response to, lost response to, or were intolerant to conventional therapy or a biologic therapy. Important Safety Information Risankizumab is contraindicated in patients hypersensitive to the active substance or to any of the excipients, and in patients with clinically important active infections (e.g., active tuberculosis). Risankizumab may increase the risk of infection. In patients with a chronic infection, a history of recurrent infection, or known risk factors for infection, risankizumab should be used with caution. Treatment with risankizumab should not be initiated in patients with any clinically important active infection until the infection resolves or is adequately treated. Patients treated with risankizumab should be instructed to seek medical advice if signs or symptoms of clinically important chronic or acute infection occur. If a patient develops such an infection or is not responding to standard therapy for the infection, the patient should be closely monitored and risankizumab should not be administered until the infection resolves. Prior to initiating treatment with risankizumab, patients should be evaluated for tuberculosis (TB) infection. Patients receiving risankizumab should be monitored for signs and symptoms of active TB. Anti-TB therapy should be considered prior to initiating risankizumab in patients with a past history of latent or active TB in whom an adequate course of treatment cannot be confirmed. Prior to initiating therapy with risankizumab, completion of all appropriate immunizations should be considered according to current immunization guidelines. If a patient has received live vaccination (viral or bacterial), it is recommended to wait at least 4 weeks prior to starting treatment with risankizumab. Patients treated with risankizumab should not receive live vaccines during treatment and for at least 21 weeks after treatment. Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been reported with use of risankizumab. If a serious hypersensitivity reaction occurs, administration of risankizumab should be discontinued immediately and appropriate therapy initiated. NORTH CHICAGO, Ill., Oct. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- AbbVie (NYSE: ABBV) today announced that new and updated data from its broad solid tumor portfolio will be presented at the 2026 European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress, taking place October 23-27 in Madrid, Spain. Spanning multiple tumor types, therapeutic modalities and stages of development, the presentations represent AbbVie's most expansive ESMO program to date. Collectively, the findings across Temab-A (telisotuzumab adizutecan), ABBV-706, ABBV-969, ABBV-1480 (RC148), alveltamig, Elahere® (mirvetuximab soravtansine-gynx) and Emrelis™ (telisotuzumab vedotin-tllv) demonstrate how AbbVie is leveraging its deep expertise in cancer biology to advance differentiated approaches that address the complexity and heterogeneity of solid tumors and help meet the diverse needs of cancer patients worldwide. "The data we are presenting at ESMO reflects the progress being made through AbbVie's disciplined, biology-driven approach to oncology innovation," said Daejin Abidoye, vice president, therapeutic area head of oncology, solid tumor and hematology, AbbVie. "Across multiple tumor types and stages of development, we are seeing encouraging evidence of longer-term clinical benefit, promising outcomes in biomarker-defined patient populations, and the potential of novel combinations and next-generation platforms. Together, these findings reinforce our strategy of translating scientific insights into differentiated treatment approaches with the potential to meaningfully improve outcomes for patients living with cancer."
